header.headline: How to Apply for an IPO in Bangladesh, Online
header.subhead: To apply for a DSE IPO, you need a BO Account. When an IPO opens, log in to the Midway Portal, apply within the 5-working-day window and pay the full subscription amount. If you are not allotted shares, your money is refunded to your BO Account.

what.title: What Is an IPO?
what.body: An IPO, or initial public offering, is when a company offers its shares to the public for the first time. Investors apply during a set window. When the offer closes, the shares are allotted and then listed on the exchange, where they can be bought and sold like other shares.

items.name: Fixed Price
items.body: The company sets one price. You apply at that price.

items.name: Book Building
items.body: Eligible institutional investors set a “cut-off price” by bidding. You apply at that price. You do not bid yourself.

who.title: Who Can Apply?

items.name: General Investor (GI)
items.body: A resident retail investor with an active BO Account.

items.name: Non-Resident Bangladeshi (NRB)
items.body: Bangladeshis living abroad have their own quota. A 1-year lock-in applies, see below.

who.note: No minimum prior stock-market investment is required to apply.

allocation.title: How the Offer Is Shared
allocation.body: A public offer is divided into quotas for different kinds of investors. The split depends on the pricing method. The two rows in blue are the ones that apply to Midway clients applying as General Investors or NRBs.
allocation.foot: Eligible Investors are institutions such as stock dealers, asset managers and merchant bankers. Source: BSEC public issue rules, Chapter VIII (Distribution and Lock-In), Rule 16.

steps.title: Apply in Four Steps

items.title: Have a BO Account
items.body: You need an active BO Account. Opening one is 100% online.

items.title: Apply in the Portal
items.body: Log in to the Midway Portal and apply while the IPO is open. The subscription window is 5 working days.

items.title: Your Money Is Held
items.body: You deposit the full subscription amount upfront. If the IPO is oversubscribed, General Investors and NRBs are allotted shares by lottery.

items.title: Shares or Refund
items.body: If you are allotted shares, they arrive in your BO Account. If you are not selected, your money is refunded to your BO Account.

steps.note: IPO applications are made in the Midway Portal, not in the QuickTrade Pro app. After listing, you can trade the shares in QuickTrade Pro.

good.title: Good to Know
items: General Investors have no lock-in. You can trade or sell shares you receive from the first trading day.
NRBs and Non-Residents have a 1-year lock-in from the first trading day at the exchange.
If an IPO is oversubscribed, allotment is by lottery, so applying does not guarantee you will receive shares.
Share prices can fall after listing as well as rise.

club.title: Never Miss an IPO
club.body: It is free to join. Sign up once in the Midway Portal, and we apply to every eligible Equity IPO on your behalf, based on your available balance. Joining is your choice, and it covers Equity IPOs only.

items.q: Do I need a BO Account to apply for an IPO?
items.a: Yes. Both General Investors and NRBs need an active BO Account. You can open one online with Midway.

items.q: Where do I apply for an IPO?
items.a: In the Midway Portal. IPO applications are not made in the QuickTrade Pro app.

items.q: Is there a minimum prior investment to apply?
items.a: No. No minimum prior stock-market investment is required to apply under current BSEC rules.

items.q: Who can apply for an IPO in Bangladesh?
items.a: General Investors, who are resident retail investors, and Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) can apply with Midway. Both need an active BO Account.

items.q: How long is the subscription window?
items.a: 5 working days. You deposit the full subscription amount upfront when you apply.

items.q: What happens if the IPO is oversubscribed?
items.a: General Investors and NRBs are allotted shares by lottery. If you are not selected, your money is refunded to your BO Account.

items.q: What is the difference between Fixed Price and Book Building?
items.a: In a Fixed Price IPO the company sets one price and you apply at that price. In Book Building, eligible institutional investors bid to set a cut-off price, and you apply at that price. You do not bid yourself.

items.q: Can I sell my IPO shares right after listing?
items.a: General Investors have no lock-in and can trade from the first trading day. NRBs and Non-Residents have a 1-year lock-in from the first trading day.

items.q: What is the IPO Membership Club?
items.a: An optional service that is free to join. You sign up once in the Midway Portal, and Midway applies to every eligible Equity IPO for you, based on your available balance.

items.q: Does applying for an IPO guarantee a profit?
items.a: No. Applying does not guarantee shares, and IPO shares can fall in price after listing. You can lose some or all of the money you invest.

cta.body: Open a BO Account online, then apply in the Midway Portal when an IPO opens. Questions? Message us on WhatsApp.

disclaimer: Investing in IPOs involves risk. Share prices can fall as well as rise after listing, and you can lose some or all of the money you invest. Applying does not guarantee an allotment, and no returns are guaranteed. Quotas, rules and eligibility are set by BSEC and the DSE and can change.
